CONTEXT. This page continues a reduction of four observations. Times are -23.25, +25.67, +84.50 and +143.28 days from an epoch. The next page is headed 'Pall.', so the body is very probably Pallas, although the previous page carries a heading about Zach's Ceres observation. Data are taken over from the previous page.
- Geocentric longitudes: α=178°33'30.34", α'=188°20'46.12", α''=181°54'2.40", α'''=176°49'50.68".
- Solar longitudes: l=74°31'15.20", l'=127°55'47.88", l''=184°14'18.38", l'''=239°43'16.60".
- Latitudes of the two middle places only: b'=11°56'32.72" (log tan b' = 9.3253237) and b''=17°43'58.82" (log tan b'' = 9.5048453).
- Log Earth distances (in the order these entries are used here): log R = 9.9582521, log R' = 9.9693112, log R'' = 9.9990438, log R''' = 9.9771377.
Using four longitudes but only two latitudes is exactly the structure of the four-observation method of Theoria Motus (1809), Lib. II, Sect. I, art. 164ff. That method is meant for orbits whose plane lies near the ecliptic. It uses the auxiliary quantities a', b', c', d', e' and a'', b'', c'', d'', e'', and iterates on the area ratios P', P'' (and Q', Q''). The page is a working draft (1805) of that machinery.

(A) Top: spherical triangle of the two auxiliary great circles. The node difference is ☊''-☊' = 137°58'43.52", half = 68°59'21.76". The first line, 126°2'47.64", is probably ☊'. If so, ☊'' = 264°1'31.16"; the top note '184.1.31.161' is probably 264°1'31.161".
- Log columns give tan u = 10^(9.5345316-9.9956277-10) = 10^(9.5389039-10), so u = 19°4'42.97" (written as 180°-160°55'17.03").
- Likewise tan v = 10^(8.5062724-7.5704935) = 10^0.9357789, so v = 96°36'47.38" (second quadrant).
- This is the Napier-analogy pattern: half-difference and half-sum of the two unknown sides.
- Then x = (v+u)/2 = 57°50'45.175" and y = (v-u)/2 = 38°46'2.205". Both are checked exactly.
- Columns 3–4 are log products of the same type:
  - 9.9276883+9.9701208 = 9.8978091;
  - 9.7966844+9.5545388 = 9.3512232;
  - 9.7260736+9.9701208 = 9.6961944;
  - 9.8919252+9.5545388 = 9.4464640.
  They lead to the angles 74°8'31.68", 60°38'2.24" and 55°14'42.80", and to the auxiliary values ξ, δ (17°51'20.79" / -1°50'59.61", then 140°43'22.63" / 82°19'25.57").
- Final arcs from the auxiliary points to the intersection D: 𝔄'D = 134°46'33.92", 𝔄''D = 13°30'29.44", B'D = -5°56'48.71", B''D = -4°20'51.35". The details of this part cannot be fully recovered from the page.

(B) Auxiliary angle P and log R. P = 58°23'57.06" with log R = 9.9933838 gives log cos P = 9.7193297 and log sin P = 9.9302966. The second P = 19°42'20.40" (replacing 18°0'21.18") with 9.9992672 gives log cos = 9.9737914 and log sin = 9.5278726.

(C) Angle differences, all checked:
- l'-α = -50°37'42.46"; α'-α = +9°47'15.78"; α''-α = +3°20'32.06"; l''-α = +5°40'48.04"; l-α = -104°2'15.14".
- α'''-l'' = -7°24'27.70"; α'''-α'' = -5°4'11.72"; α'''-α' = -11°30'55.46" (exact value 55.44"); α'''-l' = +48°54'2.80"; α'''-l''' = -62°53'25.92".

(D) Coefficient blocks. Here C. denotes the logarithmic complement and n a negative number. Two systems run in parallel: (α, α', α'') and (α', α'', α''').
1. First c-term, system 1: log[R' sec b' sin(l'-α)/sin(α'-α)] = 9.9693112 + 0.0095031 + 9.8882069n + 0.7695556 = 0.6365768n, so the term is -4.3308860.
   First c-term, system 2: log[R'' sec b'' sin(α'''-l'')/sin(α'''-α'')] = 9.9990438 + 0.0211413 + 9.1103498n + 1.0536882n = 0.1842231, so the term is +1.5283511.
   Hence c' = -4.3308860 - 0.5160758 = -4.8469618 and c'' = 1.5283511 - 0.9398502 = 0.5885009. The next page uses 0.588501.
2. d-coefficients. First, log[sin(α'-α) cos b' /(sin(α''-α) cos b'')] = 9.2304444 + 1.2343314 + 0.0116382 = 0.4764140. Likewise log[sin(α'''-α'') cos b'' /(sin(α'''-α') cos b')] = 8.9463118n + 0.6997712n + 9.9883618 = 9.6344448.
   Adding log(1+P') = 0.3429276 and log(1+P'') = 0.3011925 gives log d' = 0.8193416 and log d'' = 9.9356373. These agree with the right-hand box and are consistent with log P' = 0.0801066 (P' = 1.2026) and log P'' = 0.0003249 (P'' = 1.00075).
3. Third block: 0.0201851 = 9.9990438 + 0.0211413, i.e. R'' sec b''. Adding sin(l''-α) = 8.9955149 and 1.2343314 gives 0.2500314, i.e. 1.7784082.
   Second column: 9.9788143 = R' sec b' (9.9693112 + 0.0095031). Adding sin(α'''-l') = 9.8771249 and 0.6997712n gives 0.5557104n, i.e. -3.5950950.
   Combinations: 1.7784082 - 0.9398502 = 0.838558 and -3.5950950 - 0.5160758 = -4.1111708.
4. Constants: log[R sec b'' sin(l-α)/sin(α''-α)] = 9.9582521 + 0.0211413 + 9.9868330n + 1.2343314 = 1.2005578n. Likewise log[R''' sec b' sin(α'''-l''')/sin(α'''-α')] = 9.9771377 + 0.0095031 + 9.9494571n + 0.6997712n = 0.6358691.
   Adding log P' and log P'': 1.2806644 gives 19.083780, and 0.6361940 gives 4.3238350.
   Hence e' = -19.083780 + 0.838558 = -18.245222 and e'' = 4.3238350 - 4.1111708 = 0.2126642.
   Crossed-out values (e' ≈ -16.6, -17.0; e'' = -0.2751079, +0.1582378; 17.8658025, 3.9862046, ...) are earlier iterations with other trial P', P''.
- The right-hand box collects log a' = 9.9236804, log b' = 9.6292110, c', log d', e' and log a'' = 9.5271398, log b'' = 9.7089927, c'', log d'', e''. The next page uses them to solve for z', z'' and log r' = 0.4060200, log r'' = 0.4085368, then improves P', Q'.
- The origin of the subtracted constants 0.5160758 and 0.9398502 is not shown on this page.
errors: α'''-α' is written -11°30'55.46"; from α'''=176°49'50.68" and α'=188°20'46.12" the value is -11°30'55.44" (0.02" slip). It has no visible effect, since the log sine 0.6997712 corresponds to the correct value.
The bracket line 'sin l'-α' in the third block should read sin(l''-α). The value 8.9955149 is log sin 5°40'48.04" = l''-α.
D is written 9.9582524, but the sum 1.2005578 requires 9.9582521, the value on the previous page. Either a writing slip or a transcription issue.
The c'' entry: 1.5283511-0.9398502 = 0.5885009, and the next page uses 0.588501. The reading 0.5985009 is a misread or an overwritten slip.
Line 2 of the top block, '184 54 2.40', must be α''=181°54'2.40" (slip or misreading).
In the D' block the label 'C. cos B'' over 0,0211413 in the second column really belongs to b''. The labels are schematic, but the numbers are consistent.

results.what: Solution of a spherical triangle (sides from two nodes to the intersection of two great circles) by half-sum/half-difference (Napier) analogies with logarithms
Computation of the auxiliary coefficients a',b',c',d',e' / a'',b'',c'',d'',e'' from four geocentric longitudes and two latitudes, with iteration on the area ratios P', P''
results.modern_name: Gauss's four-observation orbit determination (Theoria Motus, Lib. II, Sect. I, art. 164ff.)

deep.surprise_reason: Numerical working draft (1805) of the four-observation method Gauss published in Theoria Motus (1809), applied to a minor planet (probably Pallas). Methodologically it is fully known as Gauss's; only the archival computational detail is new.
